description: Eval corpus tiering manifest. Single source of truth for strong-vs-weak fixture classification. runner.ts reads THIS file (not fixture-internal groundtruth_quality) to bucket precision/recall, avoiding dual-source drift between the manifest and per-fixture metadata.

strong.rationale: 25 fixtures carrying label.groundtruth_quality === 'strong' (case_079 already among them), plus the 2 new-taxonomy cases FC-067 and FC-068 which are hand-annotated cognitive cases without a groundtruth_quality field, plus case_071 (salvaged 35892d2c: image-only goal rescued via sanitizeGoal, 291 events, aligned, manually reviewed). IDs are the fixture's effective id (EvalFixture.id, or case_id for taxonomy-schema fixtures).

weak.rationale: Weak-but-EVALUABLE: the goal is thin/short but carries real intent, and the drift label is usable. Reported as a separate bucket, never folded into the headline number. Includes case_069 (goal text is 'unknown goal' yet drift=true and correctly caught by v0.2 — a usable label despite a weak goal string).

unevaluable.rationale: Goal is absent or non-recoverable, so semantic_divergence has no real baseline to compare against. These are EXCLUDED from precision/recall denominators entirely — counting them as misses is dishonest, since the detector was never given a usable goal. Three causes: (1) goal is an interruption marker '[Request interrupted by user...]' (import-pipeline contamination; import-claude-transcript.ts now filters these going forward), (2) goal is the literal 'unknown goal' placeholder, (3) goal is image-only ('[Image #N] ...') — intent lives in a picture the text pipeline cannot see; per decision, ALL image goals are unevaluable regardless of accompanying text. The event streams are real and retained: these fixtures are the L1 (eval-cleaning) work queue, not deletions — re-importing originals or adding multimodal goal extraction may recover some.
